args.name: face
args.values_note: One of the committed filenames under schema/, eg ddl.sql. Omitted, every face is printed with a `== <name> ==` banner between them so the output stays machine-splittable. Added by cc at build time (2026-08-14) alongside the search query arg.
args.note: AC-06.5 requires what this prints to be byte-identical to the committed files, which is only checkable per-face; a single blob would have to be re-split by the test to compare.

flags.help: Print each face's INTENT_VER and SCHEMA_<TYPE>_VER instead of the face bodies
flags.disposition_basis: REQUESTED BY cc (2026-08-15 17:47Z) for AC-06.10(b) / D41: _a surface reports both parts for every face, so a consumer deciding whether to upgrade can ASK rather than diff_. `keep` from the moment it is authored, because the decision is made and the obligation to read it is cc's to discharge -- `pending` would say the flag is UNDECIDED, which is the one thing it is not.
flags.ordering_note: cc asked which of us goes first and the answer is the table, which is why this row exists before the reader. **Both orderings are the EXP-05 defect in opposite directions**: reader-first makes `--versions` a flag clap REJECTS, row-first makes it a flag clap ACCEPTS and the renderer ignores. Row-first is the recoverable one -- the flag appears in `--help` and does nothing for the hours it takes cc to land the reader, and `surface_check.sh` reports it as PRESENT-vs-`keep` the entire time, so the window is INSTRUMENTED rather than merely short. Reader-first fails at the clap layer where no instrument of mine can see it.
flags.composition_with_face_arg: `--versions` selects the OUTPUT MODE; the existing `face` arg selects WHICH faces. So `intent schema --versions` prints one line per face and `intent schema ddl.sql --versions` prints that face's line only -- the two compose without a new rule, and no arm has to special-case the other. Declared here rather than left to build time because an undeclared composition is how two authors end up with two answers, which is the same defect this row's own boundary question was.
flags.spelling_note: `--versions` PLURAL, and the singular is not merely a style choice: `-V, --version` is a clap intrinsic on the root command. MEASURED 2026-08-15 -- it does NOT propagate to subcommands (`intent schema --version` gives `unexpected argument`), so the singular would not have collided today. It is still the wrong name, because it would print several lines and because a future `propagate_version(true)` would make the collision real without anyone touching this row.

new_surface.help: Extract the store into a portable format usable without Intent
new_surface.basis: design.md:57 -- YAML/md/anything else are export projections
new_surface.not_backup: SEE `backup`, which carries the full distinction. In short: this is the INTERCHANGE -- lossless text, usable without Intent, the artefact that travels between machines under D34 and reconstitutes a DB through the ingest gate. `backup` is a binary SQLite snapshot for fast local restore, carrying the derived index. Both help strings carry their own distinguishing clause deliberately, because a user choosing between them is not reading them side by side.
new_surface.truth_model_correction: 2026-08-15, ic. The help read `Project the canon into another format`, which named the DISK side as the canon and so read as one on-disk format converting to another. Under hv's ratified model the store is the truth and this command is the OPENNESS half of it -- hv, verbatim: 'I can get my data out of the db and use it somewhere else LOSSLESSLY.' The `usable without Intent` clause is in the help deliberately: AC-02.6 requires the file form to be usable without this tool, and a promise a user cannot read is a promise nobody can hold us to. This is the surface half of AC-02.6; vc owns whether the contract wants it cited on this row.

mcp_review.counterintuitive: `export` sounds like it produces a FILE and it does not -- it writes the document to STDOUT, so `intent export > estate.json` is the SHELL creating the file, not the command. Under this table's own definition the row is a `read`: `read` means no invocation of the entry, UNDER ANY FLAG, changes durable state, and this entry declares exactly one flag (`--format`, which chooses a projection) and zero arguments. Quantifying over the flag set is the whole test, and there is one flag to quantify over.
mcp_review.grounded_in: This row's own `flags` and `args`, plus `render.rs`'s `export()`, which calls the facade and `print!`s the result.

new_surface.read_or_mutate_correction: CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (ic). Was `mutate`. Found by cc while building the renderer and deferred here rather than resolved there, because the table is ic's -- `render.rs:1215` states the case in full. **The old defence was reasoned about a command that does not exist as declared**: it justified `mutate` by working-tree clobbering, which requires an output path this row has never carried. Sound reasoning, wrong subject. Two independent routes agree on `read`, which is why this is a correction rather than a preference: (1) the definition quantifies over EVERY flag, and the only flag selects a format rather than a destination; (2) `schema` is structurally the same command -- one flag, a face printed to stdout, zero destinations -- and is declared `read`, so counting shell redirection as mutation would make `schema` a mutation too and leave the table disagreeing with itself about one shape. **The MUTATE lean does not preserve the old value.** The lean governs UNCERTAINTY -- it is the tie-break when the answer is genuinely unclear -- and nothing is unclear once the flag set is read; treating a lean as a floor would make the field unfalsifiable in one direction. The cost of leaving it wrong is the failure the agent guide exists to prevent: an agent reading `mutate` treats `intent export` as capable of clobbering its working tree, and either avoids the command or copies files defensively before calling it. That is a capability the tool does not have and a workaround built against a phantom.

new_surface.help: Ingest markdown into the store through the API gate (the recovery path, and the v2 migrator)

flags.disposition_basis: RULED `keep` BY vc, 2026-08-15, on my own proposal to withdraw it -- against the proposal. It was `pending` first as half of the undeclared `sync`/`ingest` boundary (settled at `sync.boundary_ruled`: input domain, not direction), then on the narrower ground that **`--from-md` is a mode flag with ONE mode** -- reading md into the store is what `ingest` IS, so the flag distinguishes nothing. **vc: that objection is REAL and is not resolved by a table edit.** `acceptance.md` does not merely mention this flag, it RULES that the scaffolding ships in WP-03 with acceptance at AC-10.2/10.3, so **withdrawing it for tidiness would put this table in contradiction with a ratified row -- AC-05.5's exact class, which is what I caught myself about to do.** The objection belongs at AC-10.2/10.3 where its acceptance actually lands, raised against the thing itself rather than against a row describing it.
flags.why_not_dropped_by_ic: I RULED IT DROPPED AND THEN REVERSED MYSELF ON EVIDENCE, 2026-08-15, and the evidence is the point. **`--from-md` is cited outside this table in FIVE live places across FOUR artefacts I do not own**: `design.md` (design canon), `acceptance.md` (ratified -- and it explicitly says _the scaffolding still ships in WP-03_, with acceptance at AC-10.2/10.3), `parity.md` (the WP-01 register's new-in-v3 row), `WP/03/info.md`, and `intentsvcs/tests/prose_ingest_fts.rs`. Dropping it here would have made this table disagree with the ratified contract -- **the exact decision-drift class AC-05.5 was landed for an hour earlier, manufactured by me, in my own artefact, on the same day.** The command surface is mine (AC-05.1); a spelling the contract NAMES is not mine alone. Proposed to vc instead.
flags.count_corrected_twice: THE COUNT IS FIVE AND IT WAS WRONG TWICE, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE COUNT. I first wrote SEVEN and **listed six** -- an off-by-one in my own sentence, against my own list, in the same breath. cc then corrected me to SIX, because `intentsvcs/src/ingest.rs:280` genuinely stopped naming the flag under their D37 rewrite -- but cc reached six by SUBTRACTING ONE FROM MY SEVEN rather than recounting, so the correction inherited my error. **Re-measured: five.** Neither of us was careless; both of us trusted a number that had been written down. That is the same failure as every citation defect today, at the smallest possible scale. **LINE NUMBERS DELIBERATELY REMOVED FROM THIS ROW.** They were `design.md:67`, `acceptance.md:298`, `parity.md:70` -- and `acceptance.md:298` had already rotted to `:302` within the hour, because vc added rows above it. **A citation that names a line is stale as soon as anyone edits the file above it, and it goes stale SILENTLY.** This is live evidence for the AC-05.5 citation format being IDS rather than locations, which is what I proposed to vc before finding it.

args.name: path
args.values_note: A directory of markdown to read. GIVEN, that tree is ingested -- the v2 migrator's case, where the tree belongs to another project. OMITTED, this project's own markdown is ingested -- the recovery case, where you are already standing in it.
args.note: DECLARED BY ic 2026-08-15, CLOSING `input_selector_gap` below, on cc's ruling of the one part that was theirs. **The gap was that `intent ingest` had no way to say WHAT to ingest** -- measured against the built binary, `Usage: intent ingest [OPTIONS]`, one bool and no positional. I sketched the shape but did not declare it, because the arity turns on whether the recovery case DEFAULTS or REFUSES, and that is a build-time behaviour call. **cc ruled it defaults, 2026-08-15: _a migrator invoked on another tree names it; a user recovering their own estate is standing in it_** -- which is the argument from where the user's feet are rather than from symmetry, and it is right. `0..1` accordingly. cc wires it.
args.not_the_flag: This is NOT a replacement for `--from-md` and does not settle it. A bool cannot carry a path, so the arg is owed whichever way the flag question goes -- which is why it was filed as a separate finding rather than as an argument for dropping the flag.

new_surface.input_selector_gap: CLOSED at the `path` arg above (ic declared, cc ruled the default), 2026-08-15. Kept as the record of what the gap WAS: **`intent ingest` had no way to say what to ingest** -- measured, `Usage: intent ingest [OPTIONS]`, one bool flag and no positional. The recovery path and the v2 migrator both inherently take a source, and the migrator's source is ANOTHER project's tree, which cannot be implied by the working directory.
new_surface.basis: design.md:66; WP-03 deliverable, shared with the WP-10 migrator
new_surface.truth_model_correction: 2026-08-15, ic. The help read `Rebuild the canon from markdown`, which under the retracted model meant reconstructing the durable thing and so read as an authority-restoring act. Under hv's ratified model it is the opposite: markdown is a secondary artefact and ingest is the path INTO the truth, well-formed ONLY because it passes the hard gate of the intentsvcs API. `through the API gate` is in the user-facing string on purpose -- the gate is what makes the result trustworthy, so hiding it would let a reader assume a file's own format was sufficient. Recreation from an extract stays a CAPABILITY and is not a licence to treat the store as disposable.

mcp_review.why_uncertain: The recovery path and the v2 migrator behind one verb. Both are operations a human decides to run after something went wrong; neither is a task step. Closed on the strength of what it is FOR rather than what it costs.

new_surface.help: Snapshot this machine's store -- prunes expired snapshots; one-way, no restore verb ships

flags.help: List retained snapshots and when each was taken
flags.note: RATIFIED -- vc, 2026-08-15: `--list` STANDS. Proposed by ic on the grounds that D35 requires a failed or skipped backup to SURFACE, and with no read path a user cannot tell a working schedule from one that has silently never run -- the nothing-is-wrong / nothing-ran ambiguity again. **The question turned out to expose a hole in AC-03.10 itself**: the clause said only that a FAILED backup surfaces, and A SCHEDULE THAT NEVER FIRES PRODUCES NO FAILURE TO REPORT, so a green implementation could have shipped where nothing had ever run -- the ambiguity living inside the clause written to prevent it. AC-03.10 is amended and `doctor` now reports backup STALENESS, which detects never-ran without needing anything to have failed.

new_surface.basis: D35 (hv, 2026-08-15): 'a `.backup/` dir in the project that is gitignored could have a per-{day,week,month} rolled-up snapshot of the actual SQLite db file, configurable from `intent config`'.
new_surface.config: Reads `backup.enabled` / `backup.schedule` / `backup.retain.{daily,weekly,monthly}` -- named on the `config` entry in this table. `backup.enabled` gates the DAEMON's schedule and deliberately does NOT gate this command.
new_surface.not_export: *** `backup` AND `export` ARE NOT SYNONYMS, AND CONFLATING THEM COSTS A USER THE THING THEY WERE TRYING TO SAVE. *** `export` is AC-02.6 OPENNESS: lossless, text, usable WITHOUT Intent, and under D34 it is THE INTERCHANGE -- the artefact that travels between machines and reconstitutes a DB through the ingest gate. `backup` is a binary SQLite snapshot: NOT usable without SQLite, NOT the interchange, and it carries the DERIVED INDEX so a restore is immediate with no re-ingest and no re-index. Different jobs, and neither is redundant. The failure mode is directional and asymmetric: a user who reaches for `backup` when they wanted portability gets a file no other tool can read, and a user who reaches for `export` when they wanted a fast restore gets a correct artefact that costs a full re-index -- so BOTH help strings must carry their own distinguishing clause rather than relying on a reader comparing them side by side, which is exactly what nobody does at the moment they need one.

target.ratification: D35 -- the SERVICE owns the backup and both surfaces reach it. `intent backup` triggers one manually; `intentd` schedules the rolling one; ONE implementation, so CLI and daemon cannot drift into two retention policies. AC-08.8 checks that these are the SAME function, not two that agree.
target.note: The snapshot is taken with `VACUUM INTO` (or the `sqlite3_backup_*` API) and NEVER `cp` / `fs::copy` / a tar of the directory. D35 measured why: the store opens WAL, so with a writer connection still open -- exactly as a running daemon holds it -- the live DB had 50 rows, `VACUUM INTO` captured 50, and a naive `cp` captured ZERO. The `cp` result opens cleanly and reports no error, so it is indistinguishable from a good backup by inspection. That is the fabricated-stamp failure shape in a new artefact: a plausible record of something that never happened.
target.surfacing: RATIFIED -- vc, 2026-08-15: the split is the ruling. A failed or skipped scheduled backup must surface (IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001), and **`doctor` is THE ONE PLACE health is reported** -- not a second status surface here -- because `doctor` already exists for exactly that and Highlander says one place, not two. `--list` answers only _what snapshots exist_, which is inventory rather than health. `doctor`'s obligation is recorded on its own row as `target.new_obligations`, so the requirement lives where the command that owns it is described.
target.exposure: PROVENANCE EXPOSURE (ic, audit 2026-08-15; twice corrected). NOT a D42 exposure -- I filed it first for emitting a time, which is legal, and the residue is not about clocks at all. `--list` promises to show WHEN EACH SNAPSHOT WAS TAKEN and answers from the file mtime of a snapshot under .backup/db/, so a filesystem attribute is DISPLAYED AS a record fact. vc reached the identical ruling from the contract end and has absorbed it into AC-02.8: `threads.created` and `issues.created` are authored dates, `file_index.mtime` is a file mtime, `event_log.ts` was an argument, and this snapshot mtime is the fourth instance -- in all four the display was never the problem and the provenance always was. The fix is unchanged and now correctly reasoned: taking a snapshot WRITES A RECORD and `--list` reads that record stamp. Owned under AC-02.8; recorded here so the surface row carries its own obligation.

mcp_review.why_uncertain: Genuinely harmless -- it writes a snapshot into `.backup/db/` and touches nothing else. Closed only by the standing lean, which is the weakest reason on this list.

new_surface.note: ONE-WAY IS RULED, NOT AN OVERSIGHT (hv, 2026-08-17: `Backup is fine to be one-way for now`). The family ships the creating half without the undoing half and that is now a decision with a ratification rather than a gap. **The help string changed with the ruling and that is the point of recording this**: it read `Snapshot this machine's store for fast local restore`, which promised a `restore` verb that does not exist anywhere in the tool -- exactly 1 of 107 shipped rows promising a capability with no implementation, and the one my register CANNOT mechanise, because a derived detector matches a promised thing against a shipped row and this promise has no row to match. So the measurement was hand-made and the fix is a help string, not a check. `for now` is hv's word and is kept: the ruling is that no restore is owed TODAY, not that one never will be. The sibling `ext` family is one-way on different and firmer grounds -- what `ext new` creates is a directory in the operator's own HOME, so its inverse is a filesystem operation the user already owns, where a backup's inverse would have been a real capability.

new_surface.help: Serve the MCP surface over stdio

mcp_review.note: The MCP server's own launcher. Listing it inside the tool surface it serves is recursive, and an agent that can call it can spawn a second server against the same store.

new_surface.help: Reconcile the tree with .intentfiles: realise what is declared, remove what is not (previews unless --apply)

flags.help: Perform the reconciliation. Without it, organize previews and touches nothing
flags.disposition_basis: RULED BY ic, 2026-08-19, on AC-05.1, on the open row below. **`intent organize` PREVIEWS BY DEFAULT AND `--apply` PERFORMS.** The ruling rests on precedent rather than taste: AC-03.9 already settled this shape for the estate's other destructive verb -- the destructive direction states what it will overwrite BEFORE it costs it, because a summary afterwards is a receipt for a loss the operator needed one moment earlier. A second destructive verb answering the same question differently is the Highlander problem arriving in the surface. **`--apply` rather than `--dry-run`, and not only because of the default: `--dry-run` makes safety opt-in, and the operator who most needs the preview is the one who does not know to ask for it.** It also matches `organize::Mode::Apply` in the model, so surface and model spell one concept one way.
flags.measured_before_the_ruling: ic measured v3 rather than relaying it: `intent organize --help` answered `Usage: intent organize` with `-h` alone. **It had inherited v2's ACTING polarity and dropped v2's preview** -- and its own one-line help advertises `remove what is not` in the same sentence, so the destructive half was advertised and unobservable at once, with no way to learn what it would delete except by letting it. Against a real estate that was 544 planned removals.
flags.counter_argument_recorded_unsupported: `organize` is meant to be routine and idempotent, so a required flag trains reflexive typing. The usual answer -- a settled estate plans EMPTY, so the flag is only typed when there is something to do -- **does not hold on this estate today**, where 544 removals sit planned behind the AC-00.1 ship gate. It will hold once the preconditions land. ic recorded it as UNSUPPORTED rather than dismissing it, and offered to re-open on argument; dc did not take that up, because the three grounds above are about the day the gate opens and the reflex argument is about every other day.

flags.help: Write .intentfiles from status when it is absent: one STEELTHREAD line per WIP thread
flags.disposition_basis: **hv, 2026-08-26, first-hand: `--default` never removes a file -- _"Correct. Unless it is used with --force, which does remove files, after a confirm."_** ST0057 AC-11.1 through AC-11.4 are this flag's contract, and ST0057 WP-11 owns it. **IT EXISTS BECAUSE ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY.** An absent `.intentfiles` means nobody has said, so everything is realised; an empty one declares that NOTHING is, and `organize --apply` against that would remove the estate. So the file must never come into existence as a side effect, and the operator needs one spelling that writes the declaration a project should have: one `STEELTHREAD:<ID>` line per thread that is not Completed and not Cancelled. **THE SAME FUNCTION SERVES `init`, THE MIGRATION AND `upgrade` (AC-11.3), which is a criterion rather than a tidiness: three callers deriving _the open set_ separately is three chances to disagree about what open means, and the one that drifts is the one nobody runs.** `intentfiles::default_declaration` is that function. **Bare `--default` is NON-DESTRUCTIVE in every case**: absent, it writes; present, it changes not one byte, reports how many lines it declares, and names `--force`.
flags.note: narrowed off MCP as terminal-channel: --default is a different operation (declaration regeneration) whose write half is gated on a terminal confirmation via --force; the MCP tool serves reconciliation only

flags.help: With --default, regenerate an existing .intentfiles from status. Refuses without a tty; asks for confirmation on one
flags.disposition_basis: **ST0057 AC-11.2, and the tty is the mechanism rather than a courtesy: `--force` without a tty writes nothing and exits non-zero; `--force` answered `y` on a tty regenerates the file from status.** Ratified before hv's 2026-08-26 ruling and unchanged by it -- hv's _after a confirm_ lands on this row exactly. **THERE IS NO `--yes` AND NO ENVIRONMENT OVERRIDE, DELIBERATELY.** A flag-driven force without a tty WRITES, which would make AC-11.2 unmeasurable: the criterion's whole content is that the absence of a human IS the refusal, so an escape hatch does not weaken the gate a little, it removes the only thing the gate measures. **The consequence is accepted and named: no tool-driven caller can run the destructive arm** -- not the migration, not `upgrade`, not a fleet sweep. Those callers want bare `--default`, which writes a declaration and removes nothing, so nothing legitimate is blocked. **Precedent rather than invention: `int build release` already reads its confirmation from `/dev/tty`, and this estate never passes `--no-confirm` from a tool session.** With `--default` this is the destructive arm and the only one (AC-11.6).
flags.note: narrowed off MCP as terminal-channel: it qualifies --default and its whole meaning is the terminal confirmation step

new_surface.basis: D57-3 (hv, 2026-08-18): the reconciliation verb of the sparse-projection model -- hydrate, verify, dehydrate, and refuse. Implemented at `intentsvcs::organize`.
new_surface.name_reclaimed: **THE NAME IS RECLAIMED, THE v2 FACE STAYS RETIRED, AND THE TWO SHARE NOTHING BUT THE WORD** (hv, 2026-08-19). The `organize` FAMILY in this table is the v2 command -- `bin/intent_organize` plus `st organize` -- which moved ST directories into status folders, and whose ratified retire of 2026-08-14 is untouched: a strictly structured model cannot hold data in the wrong place, so the disorder it repaired cannot arise. This row is a different program that happens to take the same word: it hydrates and dehydrates artefacts against `.intentfiles`. **THREE ASSERTIONS FORBADE THE TOKEN, NOT THE FACE** -- `dispatch.rs`, `spine.rs` and `dispatch_ssot.rs` each hard-coded the string `organize`, so the ratification was expressed three times and in a form that could not tell a reclaimed name from a resurrected command. All three now key on the retired v2 ANTECEDENT, which is the thing hv actually retired.

mcp_review.grounded_in: **RULED BY ic 2026-08-30 UNDER AC-05.1, ON THIS ROW'S OWN INVITATION.** The field was carried as `uncertain` with the surface owner named rather than settled by whoever wired the entry, and it was escalated to hv, who handed it back rather than ruling it. **THE RULE THIS TABLE ENCODES IS UNDOABILITY, NOT BLAST RADIUS: MCP withholds a mutation the surface cannot UNDO.** Every removal `organize` makes is gated on the store reproducing the bytes byte for byte, so re-declaring in `.intentfiles` and re-running restores exactly what was removed. It is undoable, so it ships exposed. **THE BLAST-RADIUS ARGUMENT IS PRESERVED BECAUSE IT IS GOOD AND IT STILL LOSES.** The row's author made it first -- this is the only shipped verb that REMOVES committed files, and an agent's mistake here is an absent file rather than a bad edit -- and recorded being overridden instead of resolving it silently, which is the only reason the ruling was available to make at all. It is rejected on its own terms: the same argument would withhold `sync --to-store`, whose own row states that a wrong invocation can overwrite this machine's store from a stale extract, and which ships EXPOSED (verified against the table, not relayed from the prose). Carving an exception for one row against a rule that already decided a harder case the other way is how a vocabulary stops meaning anything. **THE `uncertain` BLOCK IS RETIRED RATHER THAN EMPTIED**, because the generator refuses an `uncertain: []` on the ground that it reads as confidence to one reader and as an unfinished edit to another; and `why_uncertain` renders only INSIDE that branch, so keeping it here would have left a key nothing reads. Its substance is above.

new_surface.flag_polarity_ruled_by_ic: **OPEN, AND DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE.** The v2 family's own notes record the defect this row must not inherit: the two v2 faces took OPPOSITE polarity for the same operation -- top-level `organize` acted by default with `--dry-run` to preview, `st organize` previewed by default with `--write` to act. That is a command-surface call and the surface is ic's (AC-05.1); hv ruled the NAME, not the flags. Recorded as an open row rather than settled by whoever wired the entry, because a polarity chosen at build time is exactly how the v2 pair came to disagree. NOTE FOR WHOEVER RULES IT: this verb REMOVES FILES, and the removal is gated on the store reproducing them byte for byte -- so the blast radius is bounded, but it is not zero, and `--dry-run`-style act-by-default puts the destructive path on the short spelling. **RULED 2026-08-19 -- see the `--apply` flag's `disposition_basis` above.** The row is kept rather than deleted because it records WHY the polarity was left open by whoever wired the entry, and that reasoning is the reason the ruling was available to be made by the node that owns the surface instead of settled silently in a commit about something else.
new_surface.hidden_aliases_basis: **hv, 2026-08-19: _we need to handle 'organise' and 'organize' but only ever show the 'z' version to keep things simple._** ACCEPTED, NEVER RENDERED -- registered with clap's `alias` rather than `visible_alias`. **A second list rather than a flag on `aliases`, because the two carry opposite reasons**: `aliases` is visible on the ground that v2 DOCUMENTS those spellings (`done|notdone`) so hiding one would be a way of not shipping it; a courtesy spelling rendered anywhere becomes a second documented name, which is the outcome this ruling exists to prevent. **THE TELL IS BUILT IN: if `organise` ever appears in any output, something is echoing the user's spelling back instead of naming the verb** -- the same class as the seventh reclaim site, where a message answered FOR a word rather than naming it. **And the same word now carries two dispositions by family: `organise` is a live hidden alias at the top level while `st organise` stays RETIRED**, which holds because `retired_refusal` walks the built surface token by token -- `st`'s subcommand `organise` is not built, so the retirement still fires there.

new_surface.help: Print the path to open for an artefact, realising it first so the path exists

args.name: kind
args.note: **THE KIND RESOLVES AN AMBIGUITY THE TOOL ALREADY REPORTS, rather than being new syntax for its own sake.** Measured 2026-08-29: `intent edit 1` refuses with `1 names both a steel thread and an issue`. AC-17.6.

args.name: id
args.note: An operator's spelling resolves to the id -- `56`, `ST0056`, `st56`, `ST56` all name one thread (AC-06.12). `address::promote` stays the one door, so a typo is a USAGE error naming both forms and never a not-found.

args.name: file
args.note: **SURVIVES THE SHAPE CHANGE, AND IT IS WHAT `--path` AND `--editor` OPERATE ON.** NO `all` -- there is no single path for it. The TUI and the browser edit the MODEL and never a file, so this argument is meaningful only under the two file-shaped modes; under the other two it is the artefact the pane would open. Carried unchanged from `st edit`, which this verb absorbs.

flags.help: Open the file in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, or in the named program, whatever stdout is
flags.disposition_basis: hv, 2026-08-29, selecting the TTY form WITH explicit overrides from three options, and superseding two earlier rulings on the same question. The bare TTY form makes behaviour depend on an invisible property of the environment, so a wrapper, a CI job or an editor plugin gets a different result with nothing in the command saying why. This is the explicit spelling of the launch branch. **THE VALUE IS OPTIONAL AND NEEDS `=`.** `--editor=code` names a program; bare `--editor` takes the resolved default. An optional-value flag followed by a positional is ambiguous to clap, and this row has three positionals. **`arity` is the register's OWN field, extended to a second position rather than minted**: it carries `0..1` on 29 of the 125 args that declare it, which is exactly this shape, and giving `flags` the same field is Highlander in its cheapest form (vc, 2026-08-29).

flags.help: Print the path and open nothing, whatever stdout is
flags.disposition_basis: hv, 2026-08-29, the other half of the same ruling. Explicit spelling of the print branch, so a caller needing determinism can say which it wants rather than depending on what stdout happens to be. **INV-10 carries the exclusion and the output contract**: `docs/getting-started.md` has `$EDITOR "$(intent st edit ST0001 design)"` under test, and command substitution makes stdout a pipe, so that invocation keeps receiving a path whatever the terminal branch becomes.

flags.help: Open the entity in the browser, served by intentd
flags.disposition_basis: **hv's opening ask names both doors** -- _the end game here is that can either: `intent edit st 68`, or browse to something like `intent browse st 68`_. **The URL addresses the ENTITY, not a filename** (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/threads/ST0058?mode=edit`): the TUI and browser edit the model, and only `--editor` opens a file -- mixing the two is what makes the current argument shape misparse. **localhost HTTP rather than a custom `intent://` scheme**: a scheme needs per-platform OS registration, buys nothing, and adds a URL-handler surface anything on the machine can invoke. **It REFUSES when the daemon is not running, naming `intent daemon start`**, rather than spawning a process the operator did not ask for.

new_surface.basis: AC-05.1 / AC-05.3. **`st edit` printed a path and left the operator to find out whether it was there** -- v2's own note says the thread DIRECTORY must exist and the file need not. Under the disk model an artefact may legitimately have no realised form at all, so the same command on a dehydrated thread names a path to nothing. **This verb hydrates first, so the path it prints EXISTS**, and `st edit` becomes a delegate rather than a second implementation: AC-05.3 is explicit that path-printing has ONE home.
new_surface.side_effect_ruled: hv, 2026-08-19. A generated view is REFUSED and the refusal NAMES THE AUTHORING SURFACE -- `acceptance.md` -> `intent ac` / `intent at`; `info.md` and WP covers -> `intent st` / `intent wp`. **Detection is not prevention**: AC-03.4 catches a hand-edited view AFTER it is written and the work is already gone. An ATTACHMENT is handed over without hesitation, because the file on disk IS the authoring surface. Derived from `Project::edit_disposition`, itself derived from `classify()`, so there is no second answer to what a file is.
new_surface.recoverability_anomaly: **WITHHELD FROM MCP WHILE BEING RECOVERABLE, AND THE GROUND IS THE RETURN VALUE RATHER THAN THE RISK.** The withhold list is derived from `recoverability` because MCP should not expose a mutation the surface cannot undo -- and this one it can: `edit` delegates to `Facade::hydrate`, idempotent in both of its steps, and adds only a read on top. **It is withheld anyway because what it RETURNS is an absolute filesystem path on this machine**, which is not merely unhelpful to a remote caller but actively misleading: a path that exists here and nowhere else, handed to something with no way to open it. The rule the list encodes is about safety and this exclusion is about meaning, so the number is left disagreeing and the reason recorded rather than the label adjusted to make it come out.
new_surface.arg_shape_change: **`edit <ADDRESS> [FILE]` BECOMES `edit <KIND> <ID> [FILE]`, AND THE OLD SHAPE MISPARSES RATHER THAN REFUSING.** `intent edit st 68` today reads `st` as the address and `68` as the file, so it refuses about the wrong thing -- which is the guess-from-shape this row exists to remove. **The terminal branch becoming the TUI is a behaviour change for every interactive user**, taken deliberately under hv's no-3.1.0 ruling: all v3 pain lands under one rubric. The register row is authored BEFORE either realiser is built (AC-17.6), so the surface decision is recorded rather than emerging from whichever realiser landed first. **THE FOUR OUTPUT MODES ARE GOVERNED BY INV-10**, which is where the mutual exclusion lives because no single flag can state it.

new_surface.help: Show the history this store holds

flags.note: narrowed off MCP as terminal-channel: it selects table-vs-json terminal rendering, and the MCP tool always answers structured JSON

new_surface.basis: The store is the event log's only home, so it is also the only route a person has to read it. Dropping the tracked extract without this verb would trade an unread projection for an unreadable table.
new_surface.not_export: SEE `export`, which is the INTERCHANGE: a whole lossless bundle for another machine or another tool. This is a READ -- filtered, ordered, for a person answering `what happened here`. The two overlap on content and not on purpose, and a person choosing between them is not reading them side by side.

new_surface.help: Fiat-close a requirement on authority, recording why -- `--because` is required and its absence refuses

args.name: target
args.note: The thread or work package, spelled with the EXISTING address forms -- `ST0001` or `ST0001/01`, `parse_wp_specifier`'s grammar. No new address form is minted for this verb: a third spelling existing for one verb would be the only place in the tool a caller addresses an entity that way.

args.name: child
args.note: Present to close a criterion or an acceptance test, as `ac satisfy` and `at edit` already spell it. ABSENT means the target itself, and AC-00.3 cascade then reaches its open children. **THE TWO CHILD KINDS ARE NOT EQUALLY WIRED, AND THE MARKER THIS ROW ANSWERS WITH IS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN SUBJECT.** Measured 2026-08-29 by ic against the debug binary, with the safe probe this row already prescribes: `fc ST9999 AC-99.9 --because <text>` reaches the arm and refuses on the unknown thread, so the AC door is WIRED; `fc ST9999 AT-99.9 --because <text>` answers `fc` is a known command that is not implemented yet, so the AT door is NOT. **The exit codes are the sharpest statement of it: rc=1 through the AC door, rc=2 through the AT door, from ONE invocation shape differing in one child prefix.** rc=2 is this tool `known command, not implemented` -- so the register now carries a row where that code is returned by a command that IS implemented, which is a FALSE instance of the meaning rather than a fifth meaning, and it is the first one measured. dc reported the cause -- the CLI arm still routes `AT-` to unwired while `Facade::at_fc` exists behind it. **The defect worth recording is not the gap but the SENTENCE: the marker names the COMMAND, and this command IS implemented.** A caller is told nothing in this build provides `fc` by a build that provides `fc`. The unwired marker has no vocabulary for a wired verb with an unwired BRANCH, and `probeable` has no vocabulary for a row that is both -- so a probe reading this row through the AC door and a probe reading it through the AT door disagree, and neither is lying. This is a member of the marker population cc is consolidating (12 files, six constants under five names) and it is the first member whose defect is the marker being WRONG rather than the marker being COPIED.

flags.help: Why this is being closed on authority rather than met -- REQUIRED

new_surface.basis: ST0066 AC-00.1, which names this path literally: `intent fc <target> --because "<text>"` fiat-closes any of the four kinds. Top-level rather than per-family because AC-00.3 makes the act CROSS-FAMILY -- an FC on an ST reaches its criteria and tests -- and a family-rooted verb writing into two other families is what family roots exist to prevent.
new_surface.acceptance: ST0066 AC-00.1 (the verb and its refusal), AC-00.3 (the cascade), AC-00.4 (renders distinguishably wherever counted)

target.no_op: DECLARED BY ic, NOT YET DRIVEN -- dc to confirm against the machine before this row is trusted. `Fiat` is not among the from-states (`computed` and `unsatisfied` only), so a second `fc` on an already-fiat-closed requirement REFUSES at exit 1 and names `ac reinstate` as the exit. Written from dc's stated machine rather than from the binary, and flagged as such: a declaration that has not been driven is a requirement, not a record.
target.kind_is_derived: The kind is read from the TARGET and is never declared. One argument matching `ST\d+` is a thread; one containing `/` is a work package; two arguments with an `AC-` second is a criterion, `AT-` a test. There is deliberately NO `--kind` flag: it would be a second home for a fact the address already carries, and that class has already cost this estate a row -- `ac new`'s `--kind` DEFAULT overwrote a stored value because clap materialises a default whether or not the caller typed it (issue 0119).
target.bare_form: **BARE `intent fc` REFUSES AT rc=1, AND rc=1 IS CORRECT -- DO NOT MAKE IT 2.** Measured by dc against a build carrying this row: `error: the following required arguments were not provided: --because <text>, <TARGET>`. A missing required argument is a USAGE error, which is rc=1 by INV-02; rc=2 means `known command, not implemented`, which is a different fact. The property ic asked for -- bare must refuse rather than dispatch to help -- HOLDS, and it holds by clap's required-args refusal rather than by the surface's own arm. That is fine and it stays true after the arm is wired.
target.refusal_has_no_structural_home: The `--because` refusal is stated in `help` because the register has nowhere else to put it. That is issue 0142's structural half, and this row is a NEW member of the population it describes -- 4 of 118 shipped rows assert a precondition in help, one of them (`at green`) measured FALSE, and the detector that found them is a regex over six English words that this row's phrasing would also evade. Recorded here so the membership is declared rather than discovered later.
target.probe_consequence: **THIS ROW CANNOT BE PROBED FOR WIRING BY DRIVING IT BARE, PERMANENTLY AND BY DESIGN, AND IT IS THE FIRST ROW OF THAT SHAPE.** `flag_reachability.rs`'s `unwired_families()` drives each probeable `new_surface[]` row BARE (`:345-362`) and asks whether the output contains `is a known command that is not implemented yet`. For a row with a required argument clap refuses FIRST, with a message that does not contain that marker, so the probe reads an unwired row as WIRED and the flag gate then fires on `--because`. **The population and the deferral path are both fine** -- `unwired_families()` walks `families` at `:249` AND `new_surface` at `:345`, and the deferral keys a `new_surface` row by its own path. **What is blind is the INVOCATION.** The fix is the rule vc drew from cc's bare-`daemon` finding the same day -- construct the probe from the row's OWN declaration rather than driving a bare form -- and for a WRITER the invocation must also be one that cannot succeed, because this same file already ruled that a probe whose question has a side effect is not a probe (the `bootstrap` incident). `intent fc ST9999 --because <probe>` satisfies clap, reaches the arm, and answers either the unwired marker or an unknown-thread refusal -- both safe, both distinguishable from each other.
target.from_states: **`computed` AND `unsatisfied` ONLY, AND `satisfied` IS EXCLUDED FOR A REASON THE REFUSAL MUST STATE** (dc reasoning, adopted here so the omission is explicable rather than arbitrary). A fiat close is how an UNMET requirement is closed on authority. Allowing it on a MET one would let a close-on-authority overwrite a close-on-evidence -- destroying the evidence in order to record that none was needed, which is the exact inversion of what the verb is for. `descoped` and `withdrawn` are excluded too, on the different ground that they are already out of scope: there is nothing to close. **THAT SENTENCE DESCRIBES THE CRITERION MACHINE AND THIS ROW REACHES FOUR MACHINES, SO IT IS A PARTIAL ANSWER SHAPED LIKE A WHOLE ONE.** The ACCEPTANCE-TEST machine entry states are `to-write` and `red` (dc, 2026-08-29, edge built and declared from those two only) -- a DIFFERENT pair naming the same idea, because a test that has not been written and a test that fails are its two unmet states the way `computed` and `unsatisfied` are a criterion two. **The token stays per-machine on purpose** -- one token for four machines is the collapse `FANS_OUT` was renamed to avoid. ST and WP have NO entry states here at all: hv ruled 2026-08-28 that neither gets a status variant and `fiat` sits BESIDE a status that stays `completed`/`done`, so the cascade reaches their CHILDREN and never moves the parent status.
target.off_scope_voice: **ic's WORDING, DECLARED AND NOT DRIVEN -- dc to wire and confirm.** Today `fc` on a `withdrawn` or `descoped` criterion answers with the bare machine refusal, where every sibling that writes about satisfaction answers with `OffScope` naming the undo. dc attempted the obvious wiring and REVERTED it, correctly: `OffScope`'s remedy hardcodes the `ac satisfy` story, so reusing it produced `if you mean to fiat-closed it` followed by a paragraph about recording evidence -- right shape, wrong sentence, and worse than the bare refusal it replaced. The sentences this row asks for, one per state: WITHDRAWN -- `error: AC-03.1 is withdrawn, so there is nothing in scope to close` / `remedy: run `intent ac reinstate <thread> AC-03.1` to bring it back into scope first. A fiat close records that an IN-SCOPE requirement was closed on authority; a withdrawn one is already out of scope, so closing it would assert something about the contract that is not true`. DESCOPED -- the same sentence with `descoped` and `intent ac rescope`. **The two differ only in the state and the undo verb, which is the whole reason they must not share one hardcoded remedy** -- that is how `ac rescope` came to be answered about `reinstate` twice (issue 0053).

mcp_review.why_uncertain: **EXPOSED, FOLLOWING THIS TABLE'S OWN DERIVATION, AND THE GROUND UNDERNEATH IT IS OPEN FOR hv.** ic first authored this row `false`: ST0066 AC-00.6 requires the LLM-side contract to FORBID invoking `fc`, so putting the one forbidden verb on the machine face hands it to the agent forbidden to use it. `gen_dispatch_table.sh` REFUSED that row, and correctly -- withholding here is DERIVED from `recoverability` (the face withholds a mutation the surface cannot undo) and `fc` is `reversible`, so withholding it asserts a ground this table does not carry. **`recoverability_anomaly` was the offered escape and ic declined it:** that key is named for recoverability, and admitting a member for a different reason is the defect this estate hit three times on 2026-08-29 alone -- `not_probed`'s `nonreturning` predecessor losing `claude upgrade` to its own name, `FANS_OUT` carrying fan-out and rename under one meaning, and this. **A key named for one reason cannot hold members admitted for another.** **AC-00.6's own text leans the same way as the derivation:** enforcement is `detection plus attribution, never a claimed impossibility`, and withholding a tool the agent can still reach by shelling out claims an impossibility it does not have. What withholding removes is the ACCIDENT, not the capability. **THE QUESTION FOR hv IS NARROWER THAN THIS ROW: does the machine face need a SECOND withholding ground -- `withheld because the loaded contract forbids it` -- distinct from irreversibility?** If yes, it is a vocabulary addition rather than a label change, and `fc` is its first member. Until then this row follows the rule that exists rather than the one ic would have written.

The cost was stated and taken: a 14th top-level family holding one leaf today.

target.roster_definition: **`surface retired` PUBLISHES `spine::retired_and_unreachable()`, WHICH IS THE SAME PREDICATE THE EXEC PATH CALLS -- not a second implementation of it.** Two doors onto one roster is the design; two answers to `is this retired` is the divergent-copy shape, in the artefact whose whole job is to stop v3 re-deriving its own surface description. **`table.retired()` ALONE IS NOT THE ROSTER and publishing it would be worse than publishing nothing:** it selects on `!is_shipped()`, which reads two declared fields and asks nothing of the built surface, so it names `organize` -- which has two rows, sits in `populations.shipped` AND `populations.retired`, and RUNS at rc=0. A caller branching on that list removes a working verb from their automation, which is the exact harm `retired_refusal`'s own comment records being measured. Mutation-proved in a detached worktree: dropping the reachability filter reds `the_enumerable_roster_excludes_a_retired_name_this_build_reclaimed` on the `organize` arm specifically.
target.why_not_an_exit_code: The row this serves previously demanded that retired and unbuilt be distinguishable BY EXIT CODE, and `spine.rs:128-131` accepts the opposite in writing. Both positions were coherent and they contradicted. hv ruled that NEITHER gives: the exit-code decision stands and the question is answered by a list. **So this verb must never acquire an exit code that encodes membership** -- that would reinstate the contradiction it was minted to resolve.
target.bare_form: Bare `intent surface` refuses at rc=1 (clap, subcommand required), as `daemon` does. **It therefore inherits the probe hazard recorded on the `fc` row:** an unwired-ness probe that drives this row BARE reads clap's refusal rather than the arm, so it cannot tell unwired from wired. The probe must construct the invocation from this row's own declared `values`, per vc's rule from cc's bare-`daemon` finding.

A tool enumerating retired verbs invites an agent to reason about surface it cannot call: actively misleading to the consumer the tier exists for.

new_surface.basis: AC-17.6, which names both verbs, and hv's opening ask, which asked for both by name. **THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE `ST0058 AC-00.6` REFUSES DISAGREEMENT, NOT DUPLICATION** -- it was driven off `intent3 --version` answering rc=0 while `intent3 version` answered the unwired marker, and two spellings that AGREE are what it asks for. new_surface.help: Open the TUI at the top of the model, or near an address if one is given

args.name: address
args.note: **OPTIONAL, AND IT IS ONE CALL TO `address::promote` RATHER THAN A SECOND RESOLVER.** `promote` tests for the `intent://` scheme itself and delegates to `address::parse`, else asks `model::normalise_id` -- so both spellings hv named reach the estate's existing one door and nothing dispatches between them. Same `address-or-id` type `edit` and `browse` already declare; the only difference is the arity. **A `/thread/ST0056` PATH SPELLING WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED**: `nav::View::parse` validates nothing (`/banana` parses as a collection), so accepting it would need new validation against `nav::kinds`, and that new validation would be the second resolver the no-address ruling was right to fear. **`intent explore 56` OPENS AT ROOT AND SAYS WHY**: untagged digits that are not exactly four are `IdError::Ambiguous`, which is the ambiguity `AC-17.6` exists to record. `ST0056`, `st56` and `ST56` resolve; `0142` is issue 142. Preferring threads for a short bare seq was rejected as a SECOND IDENTITY RULE inferring from spelling -- the class `promote`'s own doc says this table exists to kill.

new_surface.basis: hv, 2026-08-30, first-hand: _`intent explore` fires up the intent TUI at the top level ... when I do things like `intent st edit 56` I'm deep linking into an entity in the db, but I just wanted to explore it from the top._ **THE NAME IS `explore` AND NOT `browse` ON THE DESIGN'S OWN GROUNDS RATHER THAN TASTE**: `browse <kind> <id>` already ships meaning _open in the BROWSER_, and one word carrying two meanings on one surface is the defect `tui-design.md` section 5 records for `Up`/`Down` and section 4 for `/`-as-both-menu-and-prefix. **IT TAKES AN OPTIONAL ADDRESS, RULED BY hv 2026-08-30**, superseding vc's no-address ruling of the same day, which was made while hv was AFK. **The superseded text is DELETED rather than banner-marked**, per `restart.md`'s own rule about supersedes banners. hv, verbatim: _I see no reason why `intent expl[ore] ...` couldn't take an `intent://...` URL scheme URI or even an ID that it tries to match to something if it can, and if it can't it just opens at the root. That doesn't obviate `intent edit ...` in any way. It's just convenience for the user as they need._ **THE THREE-DOORS OBJECTION DOES NOT REACH IT, AND THE GROUND IS IN THIS TABLE RATHER THAN IN AN ARGUMENT**: `edit` and `browse` ALREADY declare their `id` as `address-or-id` carrying the note _`address::promote` stays the one door_, so `explore` reuses that word and that door and differs only in arity. Deep linking remains `edit`'s job; this is the browser opening NEAR a thing rather than acting ON one, which is why the two verbs diverge on the miss: **`edit ST9999` must REFUSE because it was asked to act on a specific thing, and `explore ST9999` opens at the root because it was asked to open the explorer.** **AND THE FALLBACK ANNOUNCES ITSELF.** hv said _it just opens at the root_; the honest form is the root PLUS the reason on the info row, because a browser that silently opens somewhere other than you asked is the answer-confidently-from-partial-evidence class v3 exists to remove. **THERE ARE FIVE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO**, and they must read differently: it resolves and is present; it resolves and is ABSENT (`ST9999` -- `promote` is purely syntactic and never reads the store, so a landing computed from the grammar alone paints a blank form, which is reachable-and-blank reading as data); it is a REAL address whose form has no view (`intent:///nodes/vc` -- six of thirteen `Entity` forms have views); it names TWO things (`1`); it names nothing (`banana`). **`explore` IS NOT A SECOND SUBSYSTEM -- it is the same view stack with a different BOTTOM**, rooted at the entity kinds rather than at one item, which is why the whole addition is a verb rather than a realiser.

mcp_review.grounded_in: Withheld because the channel cannot carry it, not because the mutation is unsafe -- the full argument and its precedent are in `recoverability_anomaly`, which is the field the generator reads and therefore the one home for it. What still mutates, since the row takes no arguments and ships no flags: the TUI writes through the facade on `Enter`, and the surface it offers is the form declaration rather than this command line.
mcp_review.note: The browser twin of this reach is `edit --browser` / `browse`, which is also `exposed_on_mcp: false`. Both are HUMAN faces onto the same model; the agent's door onto that model is the daemon's JSON face (AC-08.9), not either realiser.

new_surface.recoverability_anomaly: **WITHHELD FROM MCP WHILE BEING REVERSIBLE, AND THE GROUND IS THAT IT IS NOT CALLABLE RATHER THAN THAT IT IS DANGEROUS.** The withhold list is derived from `recoverability` because MCP should not expose a mutation the surface cannot undo -- and this one it can: every edit `explore` makes goes through `intentsvcs` like any other client and is reversible by the same doors. **It is withheld because an interactive TUI blocks on keystrokes and needs a terminal, so an agent calling it receives a request that never returns.** That is a fact about the CHANNEL, not about the risk. **IT IS THE THIRD ROW ON THIS EXACT GROUND AND THE PRECEDENT IS WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ARGUED**: `edit` and `browse` are both reversible, both withheld, and both on the ground that what they reach is a HUMAN face on THIS machine -- a path or a URL that exists here and nowhere else. `explore` is the third face in that set and the agent's door onto the same model is the daemon's JSON face (AC-08.9), not any of the three. **Recorded rather than resolved by relabelling: calling it `one-way` would make a derived number come out and would be false**, which is the move the `daemon` head row was making while one row stood for four verbs. Same day, ic ruled `organize` EXPOSED under AC-05.1 on the converse reasoning -- blast radius is not the rule, undoability is -- so bending undoability here to cover a channel problem would have contradicted a ruling made hours earlier.

new_surface.basis: hv, 2026-08-30, ruling `help` INTO the 3.0.0 cut at the ROOT ONLY. The `help` FAMILY's `target.spelling_note` already scheduled exactly this -- _the v2 face stays retired and the TOKEN is reclaimed by a new program, declared in `new_surface`_ -- so this row lands a ruling the table had been carrying as pending since 2026-08-26. hv's fuller `<cmd> help` shape (man-style `.md` on the WHY/WHAT while `<cmd> --help` keeps the params/HOW) is RECORDED AND POST-TAG; it is not what this row ships.
new_surface.acceptance: ST0058 AC-00.6 (driven by vc 2026-08-30). The row's falsifier is _any capability reachable by a flag and refused by its subcommand twin, or the reverse_, and `intent --help` rc=0 against `intent help` rc=2 was its last live instance -- issue 0086.
new_surface.name_reclaimed: **THE NAME IS RECLAIMED, THE v2 FACE STAYS RETIRED, AND THIS FOLLOWS `organize` EXACTLY.** The `help` FAMILY in this table is `bin/intent_help`, whose retire is untouched and whose reasons are unchanged: `lib/help/` held 11 help files for 27 commands, its grammar was used once each, and it hand-maintained a command list behind a skip list rather than enumerating the surface. **None of that is ported.** The token is taken by a different program: a spelling of the help clap already renders from the compiled-in dispatch table. **AND `spine.rs` FORBADE THE TOKEN RATHER THAN THE FACE** -- `.disable_help_subcommand(true)` -- which is the same three-assertions shape `organize` hit.
new_surface.one_home: **THIS SHIPS NO HELP TEXT OF ITS OWN, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** The arm rebuilds the clap `Command` from the same compiled-in table `--help` uses and asks IT to render, so the twin AC-00.6 is about cannot drift apart later -- there is one renderer with two spellings. The estate already carries three homes for _what is Intent_ (`--help`'s command list, `intent llm`'s generated agent guide, `intent info`'s install-and-project status); **a fourth authored page would have been the Highlander violation this row exists to avoid**, and writing one is what `bin/intent_help` did.
new_surface.root_only: **ROOT ONLY, AND THE ARG IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT** (hv, 2026-08-30). The v2 `help` entry declared `command` at arity `0..1`; this row declares no args, because the live twin-pair AC-00.6 fires on is the ROOT one and per-command help already answers as `intent <cmd> --help`. Declaring the arg here would ship a third spelling of per-command help while hv's post-tag `<cmd> help` is a DIFFERENT surface with different content, and the table would then carry a promise the post-tag ruling has to unmake.
new_surface.recoverability_absent: **DECLARED ABSENT, NOT OMITTED.** `help` is a `read`, and `dispatch.rs`'s vocabulary check refuses a recoverability on one -- _the question is vacuous for a command that changes nothing_. Recorded here so the absence reads as the rule rather than as an oversight, which is the table's own standing objection to absence-as-meaning.

coverage_findings.finding: NOTHING in the BATS estate invokes `intent config`. Zero files, zero tests.
coverage_findings.why_it_matters: This family already has no v2 behaviour to be faithful to (0B on both streams, exit 0) and now also has nothing that would notice a change. Both halves of the safety net are absent at the same site: v3 can do anything here and the suite stays green. It is the strongest possible argument for the `undefined` class being separate from `corrected` -- there is neither an antecedent nor a guard.
coverage_findings.trap: `tests/unit/config.bats` EXISTS and burns 5 of 7, which makes the hole invisible in any file listing. It tests config LOADING -- through `intent info`, `intent doctor` and `intent st list` -- and never invokes `intent config` once. A file named after a command that does not test that command is worse than no file, because it answers the question 'is this covered?' wrongly and confidently.
coverage_findings.action: WP-06 must land a conformance test for `intent config` BEFORE changing its behaviour, or the `undefined` ruling is unverifiable by construction.

coverage_findings.finding: 2 burning tests. `tests/unit/fileindex_commands.bats` holds 47 tests and 45 of them bypass the dispatcher entirely.
