coverage_findings.finding: The zero for `config` was calibrated before being believed: the same needle returns 3 files for `doctor` (a known-covered control), and a direct grep for `intent config` / `run_intent config` returns nothing.
coverage_findings.why_it_matters: A measuring instrument that reports zero is indistinguishable from a broken one until it is shown to report non-zero somewhere it should. This is the calibration rule that came out of the zsh probe artefact earlier in the same session, applied to the very next instrument built.

coverage_findings.finding: Three rows carried `evidence_class: measured` on a probe matrix that could not have reached the field they filled. The matrix is bare / --help / unknown flag / outside-a-project -- four invocations, no positional argument -- and `issues add`, `wp list` and `critic` each REQUIRE an argument to succeed, yet each declared a success-path `stdout`. Found by cc on `issues add` while reading v2 for Machine 4; generalised and bounded to three by ic the same day.
coverage_findings.why_it_matters: **An `evidence_class` names a METHOD, and nothing checked that the method reached the fields the row went on to assert.** The class was honest -- it says exactly which four invocations were run -- so the defect is not dishonesty but an unstated coverage claim: a reader takes `measured` as being about the ROW, when it is only ever about the PROBE. That is the same shape as a criterion stated more broadly than the one applied, which is what cost `populations.not_probed` a member the day before. It is also why the count matters: the first reading of this was 25 rows, and 22 of those are fine because bare IS their success path (`issues`, `todo`, `info`, `version`, the usage-block families). Only a row whose success needs an argument is exposed.
coverage_findings.trap: `measured` outranks `read` in every reading, so the three exposed rows looked like the BEST-evidenced rows in the table. `issues add` in particular carried a four-invocation matrix in its own `why`, which reads as diligence and is precisely the text that should have raised the question.
coverage_findings.action: All three now carry a direct observation of the success path alongside the matrix, and one of the three was WRONG when measured (`critic` declared only the findings report; the clean case prints a one-line `ok:` summary). No sweep beyond the three: the discriminator is `a required arg the matrix never supplied`, and it is mechanical, so it can be re-run rather than remembered.

known_exposures.title: The generated view is formatter-stable today by accident, not by design
known_exposures.detail: cc found a third formatter class: prettier normalises the AUTHOR's own emphasis (`*major*` -> `_major_`). No renderer discipline can reach it, because a renderer is forbidden to rewrite authored prose -- and the prose here comes from the canon. This view currently contains ZERO single-asterisk emphasis spans, measured, so it does not trip the class. That is luck: one canon note written with `*emphasis*` breaks the skew check on this file tomorrow, and the break would look like drift on a file nobody touched.
known_exposures.resolution: AC-07.6 (vc, 2026-08-14): generated views are EXCLUDED from the formatter repo-wide, converged at `init` and migration so consumer repos inherit it -- a local `.prettierignore` would fix this tree and leave the shipped skew check crying wolf in Lamplight, Utilz and Baize forever. Deliberately not landing today: the pre-commit hook rewrites every staged `.md` and `git add`s it, and three nodes hold uncommitted work.
known_exposures.it_happened: PREDICTED HERE, THEN IT HAPPENED, 2026-08-15. This entry said the zero-emphasis state was LUCK and that one canon note written with single-asterisk emphasis would break the skew check on a file nobody touched. I wrote FOUR that afternoon; the view stopped being a fixed point of the formatter; the commit gate refused; and the message it refused with -- `the committed view is stale, or a row was hand-edited` -- named neither cause, so it cost a long diagnosis. **An exposure register that correctly predicts a defect and does not prevent it has done half a job**, and the half it did is the cheaper one. `gen_dispatch_table.sh` now REFUSES a render that is not a fixed point of the formatter, naming the offending lines, which closes the mechanism half without waiting on AC-07.6 and without a renderer rewriting authored prose. AC-07.6 remains the right repo-wide fix; this is the local control that should have existed when the exposure was first written down.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: The table aligner has TWO justifications and only one of them expires. (1) The skew justification -- matching the formatter's column widths so regeneration reproduces the committed bytes -- becomes unnecessary the moment AC-07.6 lands. (2) The house-rule justification -- `in-standards`: all markdown tables must be column-aligned -- does not expire, and the formatter was correcting a real defect rather than imposing a preference. So the aligner STAYS after AC-07.6; what goes away is the need for it to match the formatter's choices exactly. Written down because a future reader finding align logic in a renderer whose output the formatter no longer touches would reasonably assume it was vestigial and delete it.

known_exposures.title: Two artefacts now describe the command surface, and nothing checks they still agree
known_exposures.detail: `parity/cmd-<command>.md` (26 files, GENERATED by `gen_inventory.sh` from probes and static passes) and this file (AUTHORED) both carry the verb and flag sets. They were built in that order -- the table was derived from the inventory plus per-arm source reads, then enriched with target / disposition / invariants -- so it is a derive-then-enrich relationship rather than a copy-paste, which is normal and fine. What is NOT fine is that nothing keeps them in agreement afterwards. Spot-checked at the stamped revision: `lang`, `plugin` and `modules` agree exactly (the inventory lists `rm` as its own row where this file records it as an alias on `lang remove` -- consistent, differently represented). Agreement today with no mechanism is the divergent-copy shape, and it is the shape THIS artefact exists to eliminate elsewhere in the surface. Named against my own work rather than left for someone else to find.
known_exposures.resolution: The next re-sweep re-runs `gen_inventory.sh`, which regenerates the 26 inventory files from live measurement. **That pass must include a drift check between the regenerated verb/flag sets and this file's**, and a disagreement must be reported rather than resolved by picking a winner: the inventory is measurement and this file is judgement, so a divergence means either the surface moved or a judgement here was wrong, and those need different responses. Without that check the re-sweep silently updates one of the two descriptions and leaves the other stale, which is worse than today's position -- they agree now.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: None; the drift check belongs to the inventory toolchain, not the renderer. Recorded here because this file is the one that would be silently wrong.
known_exposures.update_2026_08_15: The drift check EXISTS (`parity/tools/drift_check.sh`) and runs clean across 26 families, so the mechanism half of this exposure is closed. What EXP-02 did not anticipate is that the two artefacts are not equally checkable: the inventory's own input (`probes/toplevel.tsv`) was never tracked and is now gone, so the MEASUREMENT side cannot be content-checked at all and rests on its stamp. The drift check compares this file against an artefact nobody can currently re-derive. See `parity.md`'s rule on artefacts that cannot be re-derived from committed state.

known_exposures.title: Two ACs say the MCP tool tier and the agent guide are GENERATED from this file, and this file cannot answer the first question either generator will ask
known_exposures.detail: AC-09.1 -- _the typed tool tier is generated from the dispatch table_ -- and AC-09.4 -- _`intent llm` renders the agent guide from the dispatch table; NO HAND-MAINTAINED COMMAND LIST EXISTS_. Measured 2026-08-15 against all 103 rows: **no row says whether it is exposed on the MCP surface, and no row says whether it reads or mutates.** Neither fact is derivable from what is here. `observed.side_effects` exists on 10 rows of 103, so its absence means `not recorded`, not `no side effects` -- reading it as a read/write flag would be absence-as-meaning in the one place it decides whether an agent may close a steel thread. Nothing is broken today because WP-09 has not started; the exposure is that the ACs already assume a capability this artefact does not have.
known_exposures.why_it_bites: A generator that must decide per command, from a table that does not say, has exactly two options and both are defects. Expose EVERYTHING and `intent mcp` becomes a tool that starts an MCP server from inside one, alongside `daemon` and other commands with no agent-facing meaning. Or carry a skip list in the generator -- **which is a hand-maintained command list living one command away from the AC that forbids hand-maintained command lists**, and it is the designed-figure shape as well: correct when typed, silently wrong at the next command added, because the act that invalidates it (ic adds a row) is not the act that updates it. The identical argument settled `config set`s valid-key set the same day.
known_exposures.second_missing_fact: Read-versus-mutate is not cosmetic on an agent surface. `st list` and `st done` would be indistinguishable tools to a client that has only a name and a description, and one of them closes a steel thread. AC-09.5 already separates read surfaces as MCP RESOURCES, so the distinction exists in the contract and simply is not in the table for the tool tier to honour.
known_exposures.resolution: Two declared fields per entry -- exposed-on-MCP, and read-or-mutate -- **declared per row rather than derived from the verb**, because deriving from a name is the sniffing this toolchain keeps refusing (`st sync` and `sync` are different commands sharing a spelling; `ac gate` reads while `wp done` consults the same gate and writes). Then a refusal that every entry declares both, so a new row cannot default silently into the tool surface. NOT landed unilaterally today: adding the fields is authoring, which is ic's, but CLASSIFYING 103 rows is a judgement with a safety edge and belongs with vc and cc as WP-09 opens. Raised now, before WP-09 starts, so it is a specification rather than a rediscovery -- the same row-before-surface order that worked for `ac unsatisfy` and the seven lifecycle verbs.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: None yet. When the fields land, the completeness refusal already added to `gen_dispatch_table.sh` will carry them into the view for free, because it renders every authored field rather than an enumerated set.

known_exposures.title: A `keep` disposition is honest about the SURFACE and silent about the SEMANTICS
known_exposures.detail: vc, 2026-08-15, generalising from `st new -s|--start`. The whole disposition vocabulary -- `keep · retire · deviate · corrected · new-surface · pending` -- classifies what happens to a COMMAND'S SURFACE. It has no way to say _the spelling, the flags and the observed behaviour are all unchanged, and the meaning moved anyway_. That is exactly what happened to `-s|--start`: it is v2 parity, its help text still matches, its v2 behaviour still matches, and **a ratified decision changed the state space underneath it** so that one transition became two. **Nothing in this file could have shown that**, and a reader scanning dispositions would have seen `keep` and moved on.
known_exposures.why_it_will_recur: The trigger is not a surface edit, which is what this table watches; it is a RATIFIED MODEL CHANGE landing elsewhere -- in `data-model.md`, in the state machines, in an enum collapse. So the invalidating act happens in a file this artefact does not read, performed by a node that is not editing this artefact. **Two more machines have already been ratified and WP-06's verbs are still landing**, so instance one is not instance last. It is the same structural shape as a hand-maintained roster going stale: the act that invalidates it is not the act that updates it.
known_exposures.resolution: **Deliberately NOT solved today, and vc explicitly did not ask for a mechanism.** Recorded here rather than left as a note in an inbox because an inbox entry gets archived and this section is read by anyone who reads the table -- and because the honest status of this exposure is _known, unprotected_, which is precisely what `known_exposures` exists to say. The cheap partial already in use: when a row's semantics move under a ruling, say so ON the row in its own field (`st new` now carries `start_flag_ruled` and `composition_constraint`), so the fact is at least greppable even though the disposition cannot carry it. If it recurs often enough to need a mechanism, the shape is a semantics stamp -- the ruling a row was last checked against -- and that is a contract decision for vc, not a renderer change.

known_exposures.title: Entries declare whether they ship; FLAGS could not -- CLOSED in this file, still open in the spine
known_exposures.detail: `is_shipped()` reads an entry's `disposition` and `target.state`, so a retired COMMAND never reaches clap. There is no equivalent one level down: `spine.rs` builds every declared flag on every shipped entry, unconditionally, and the flag schema carries no field that could say otherwise -- measured, the union of all flag keys across this table is: accepts, default, help, note, required, spellings, type, value. So the table can withdraw a command from the v3 surface and CANNOT withdraw a flag. That is the structural gap behind AC-06.8, and it is the same shape as EXP-03: a fact a generator needs, that this file does not carry, and that cannot be derived -- whether a flag is READ is a property of the renderer, never of its spelling.
known_exposures.it_happened: Measured 2026-08-15 (ic) against the BUILT BINARY, not read off the source. `intent doctor` declares --fix, --verbose and --quiet; `fn doctor()` takes no ArgMatches and its dispatch arm discards them, so it cannot read any of the three even in principle. All four invocations -- bare, --fix, --quiet, --verbose -- produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output, while `intent doctor --help` prints 'Attempt to fix issues automatically'. AC-06.8 calls a declared-and-inert flag a lie told by --help; AC-06.9 says doctor --fix is specified before it is wired OR withdrawn from the surface, and records that cc declined to wire it and was right to. BOTH ACs already forbid this and it shipped anyway, because withdrawal had no mechanism: declining to wire it was the whole of the action available.
known_exposures.resolution: CLOSED HERE, AND ONLY HERE. EVERY flag declares a disposition -- **the count is deliberately not written here.** It said `All 93 flags (63 keep, 14 retire, 10 intrinsic, 6 pending)` and went stale the first time a flag was added, which was `schema --versions` on 2026-08-15, hours later. **A tally in prose is a hand-maintained roster inside the artefact that exists to abolish hand-maintained rosters** -- the same shape as AC-02.6's eight-vs-nine table list, and the reason that one is now enumerated from the generated face. The live numbers come from the file: `jq '[.families[].entries[], .new_surface[]] | map(.flags // []) | add | group_by(.disposition) | map({(.[0].disposition): length}) | add'`. Three refusals enforce it, and a shared renderer plus a COUNT-based check puts every one of them in the view. THE SPINE DOES NOT YET HONOUR IT: `spine.rs:142` still builds every declared flag on every shipped entry, so today the declaration is documentation with a guard on it. That half is cc's and the first user is `doctor --fix`, whose `retire` is the one classification vc measured in v2 source rather than inferred. Until it lands, this file can say a flag does not ship and the binary will ship it -- which is a smaller gap than not being able to say it at all, and is not the same as closed.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: Nothing yet: the generator renders flags faithfully and has no opinion about whether they ship. It gains one the moment the field exists -- every flag must declare a disposition or the run refuses, the same construction as the MCP fields, so a flag cannot join the surface by being typed. Until then this register is the only place the gap is written down. The 44 further declared-and-unread flags all sit on commands with NO renderer arm at all, so they are future violations rather than current ones: they become AC-06.8 breaches one at a time as each command is wired, which is the worst arrival schedule available for a defect nobody is watching for.

known_exposures.title: D42 audit of the declared surface: it came back CLEAN, and the two findings that survive are not about clocks
known_exposures.detail: Audited the dispatch table and the 27 command inventories against D42 and filed three findings. hv then narrowed the rule twice within the day and BOTH narrowings cut against me. First: the rule is ASYMMETRIC -- no CLI or intentsvcs function TAKES a time, but functions may RETURN times, because those went end-to-end through the DB where SQLite set them; vc has since sharpened this into its strongest form, a property of the SIGNATURE rather than of a value, so a time-typed input parameter is a defect by inspection and nobody has to trace provenance. Second: reading a clock to MAKE A DECISION is fine, and so is stamping WHEN A COMMAND RAN into a GENERATED artefact -- what D42 forbids is confecting a time and injecting it into a source document. Under the rule as it now stands the declared surface has NO D42 exposure at all: zero of three findings survive as D42, and the inventories were already clean because v2 declares no time-bearing flag or argument anywhere.
known_exposures.it_happened: The audit was still worth running, because two of the three findings turned out to be real defects of a different kind and one of them is only visible from here. `doctor` staleness is WITHDRAWN outright -- comparing snapshot age against a schedule is a decision, which is the permitted case, and nothing durable is written. `backup --list` is NOT a clock defect but a PROVENANCE one, displaying a file mtime as a record fact; vc ruled the same thing from the contract end and it is now AC-02.8's fourth instance. `todo done --flush` is the one that pays for the exercise: chasing my own D42 claim into bin/intent_todo to check it showed the watermark is read BACK OUT of the generated todo.md, so a generated view is the sole store of durable state -- which the v3 truth model, where deleting a derived artefact is always safe, turns from a wart into a data-loss path. Both survivors are recorded on their rows as `target.exposure`; the `d42_exposure` key is GONE, because a census key with no members and a wrong name is worse than none.
known_exposures.resolution: None adopted here; each row names its own owner (`todo done` is WP-03's renderer constraint, `backup` is AC-02.8). The finding worth keeping is about auditing, not about time. THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT TO RUN AND WRONG IN EVERY VERDICT IT FIRST REACHED, and it still produced two real defects -- because the only way to check a claim about a surface is to read the code under it, and the reading is what found them. An audit that had trusted its own pattern match would have filed three wrong findings and stopped.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: None today; the generator renders `exposure` through the generic `targetextra` path like any other authored sub-key, and the entry-level completeness check proves it reaches the view. Two standing obligations, and they are different sizes. The small one: re-audit when new_surface changes. The large one: THIS CENSUS CANNOT SEE THE THING THE RULE ACTUALLY FORBIDS. vc's caution is exact -- a clean result here is about DECLARED FLAGS AND ARGUMENTS, and hv's rule is about function PARAMETERS, which need never appear in a flag inventory. A green from this file is not evidence about signatures, and the needle that checks them lives in cc's guard, not here.

known_exposures.title: The flag schema declares five properties the CLI cannot see, and one of them is a live defect on an implemented command
known_exposures.detail: Measured while classifying for EXP-05, by reading `dispatch.rs` rather than reasoning about the renderer. `pub struct Flag` at dispatch.rs:126-133 has exactly THREE fields -- `spellings`, `kind`, `help`. The canon authors eight: those three plus `accepts` (4 instances), `default` (6), `required` (3), `value` (35) and `note` (9). So `accepts`, `default`, `required` and `value` DO NOT DESERIALIZE AT ALL. This is not a renderer that forgets to read them; it is a type with no field for them, which is the same shape EXP-05 diagnosed for `disposition` -- except EXP-05 said the schema was missing ONE field and the measurement says it is missing FOUR that are already authored.
known_exposures.it_happened: `required` is the one that bites, and all three instances land differently, none of them driven by the declaration. `ac satisfy --evidence` is declared `required: true` and read as `arg(a, "evidence").unwrap_or_default()` (render.rs:671), so a missing `--evidence` SILENTLY BECOMES THE EMPTY STRING and the criterion is satisfied with no citation -- on an implemented command, today. `ac descope --to` and `ac withdraw --reason` ARE enforced, by `?` in the renderer (render.rs:715, :727), which is the right outcome reached at the wrong layer: clap never sees a required argument, and `ac withdraw --reason`s own help text says REQUIRED. Three declarations, three fates, and the table's claim caused none of them. `accepts` is worse in kind if not in effect: four enum domains are declared and unvalidated, so `--severity-min banana` parses. `value` is a metavar clap supports and the spine already uses for positional args (spine.rs:131) but never for flags. And separately from the struct: `spine.rs:152-159` SILENTLY DROPS any flag with no long spelling -- `claude subagents -v`, `claude skills -v`, `fileindex -r`, `fileindex -v` are declared here and reach no surface at all, via a bare `continue` with no diagnostic, which is IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001 in four instances.
known_exposures.resolution: Not adopted here, and deliberately NOT folded into EXP-05. EXP-05 was ruled as a specific mechanism and vc anchors review to the proposal, so widening it silently while implementing it is the way a reviewed change becomes an unreviewed one. Recorded whole instead. The cheap half is this file's and is already done -- `default` and `required` now RENDER, so a reader of the view can at least see the claim. The rest is cc's: four fields on `Flag`, `.required()`/`.default_value()`/`.value_parser()`/`.value_name()` on the clap side, and a refusal rather than a `continue` for a flag the spine cannot build. `ac satisfy --evidence` is the one worth doing first because it is live and silent.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: Two, both now closed. The flag level was the LAST population with an enumerated renderer and no generic remainder -- `extras` had closed the entry and `target` levels and nothing descended into `flags` -- so `default` and `required` had been in the canon and out of the view for as long as they had existed, and no check anywhere could say so. `flagextra` closes it. The second is sharper and is a lesson about checks rather than about flags: the flag completeness loop I wrote to close this class WENT GREEN ON ITS FIRST RUN while five flags rendered nothing, because it greps for the LABEL and 88 of 93 flags supplied it. Presence-of-label and completeness-of-population are different questions. It is now a COUNT, matched against the declared total, and the count is what found the fact that new_surface flags had never rendered in detail at all.

known_exposures.title: The root command's help is the one help string in the surface that does not come from this file
known_exposures.detail: This file's own `about` opens by claiming that the clap surface, THE HELP TEXT, the MCP tool list and the `intent llm` agent guide all render FROM it. Measured 2026-08-16 and it is true 107 times out of 108. `spine.rs` sets `.about(entry.help)` for every family, entry and verb, and `.help(flag.help)` for every flag -- so help is table-driven BY CONSTRUCTION for the whole command surface, which is also why the SSOT test spot-checking a single command (`st new`) is defensible rather than thin. The exception is `spine.rs:26`, the ROOT command, whose about is a Rust string literal: `Intent: steel threads, work packages and the acceptance contract`. It is the only `.about(` literal in the entire CLI, and grepping this file for that sentence returns zero. **It is also the first line an agent reads from `intent --help`.** The general shape is the one this contract has hit from four sides in one day: an artefact asserting a property it very nearly has, where the near-miss is invisible because the assertion is true everywhere the reader checks.
known_exposures.why_it_is_not_merely_tidiness: AC-09.4 renders the agent guide from this table and forbids a hand-maintained command list. A guide needs a one-line statement of what the tool IS, and there is nowhere in this file to render it from -- so the guide must either hard-code that sentence, which is the second set of strings the AC exists to abolish, or omit it. The gap is invisible today precisely because nothing renders the root yet; it becomes a defect the moment WP-09 starts.
known_exposures.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-16, both halves in one commit. `root_help` is declared here and `spine.rs:26` reads it, so there is no longer a `.about(...)` string literal anywhere in the CLI and this file's `about` claim -- that the clap surface and THE HELP TEXT render from it -- is true without exception. Landed by ic across both halves rather than waiting for the handoff, on hv's steer of 2026-08-16 (`the sooner we can get this project onto v3, the better`) and because `spine.rs` was clean while cc was working elsewhere; raised with cc the same minute with an offer to revert if they would rather own the wiring. **The sequencing constraint that shaped this is still the right one and was not waived: the field was never declared while nothing read it**, because a declared value nothing renders is exactly what AC-06.8 exists to prevent -- the two halves landed together, which is what the constraint asks for, rather than the field landing first and waiting.
known_exposures.it_happened: The field is NOT `#[serde(default)]`, and that is the lesson from this entry applied to its own fix. A defaulted empty string would render `intent --help` with a blank about line, which reads as a styling choice rather than a missing value -- the silent-empty class this whole contract spent 2026-08-16 removing, in five separate instruments. A table without the key now refuses to load.

known_exposures.title: The ROOT intrinsics are on the surface and NO row declares them -- and `--version` swallows every argument after it at exit 0
known_exposures.detail: `-V` / `--version` and the root `--help` reach the surface of the shipped binary and **no entry in this table declares them.** The `version` SUBCOMMAND row is a different thing and declares `flags: []`; the ten flags carrying `disposition: intrinsic` are all `--help` / `-h` on named commands. The only place the root `-V` is written down at all is a prose `spelling_note` on `schema --versions`, which mentions it to explain why that flag is plural. **So the register describes a binary whose first-typed surface it does not cover.**
known_exposures.it_happened: MEASURED 2026-08-17 (ic) against the BUILT BINARY at `native/rust/target/debug/intent`, prompted by cc asking whether build metadata should extend `intent --version --verbose` or take a new dispatch row. The answer was neither, because there is no row to extend. **`--version` SHORT-CIRCUITS BEFORE ARGUMENT VALIDATION AND SWALLOWS EVERYTHING AFTER IT AT EXIT 0**: `--version --verbose`, `--version --zzz`, `--version NOSUCHTHING` and `-V --zzz` all print `intent 3.0.0-dev` and exit 0. `--help --zzz` does the same. **The subcommand is correct and the root is not** -- `version --verbose` exits 1 with `unexpected argument`, as does `--verbose --version` when the flag comes first, so the swallow is specifically the clap `DisplayVersion` / `DisplayHelp` action firing during parse and exiting before the unknown-argument check. **THAT IS INV-02 UNMET ON THE ROOT COMMAND**, and the `version` row's own `target.behaviour` asserts the opposite in as many words: `Unknown arguments refused, exit 1 per INV-02`. True of the row, and the row is not what the user types first. **THE FIRST MEASUREMENT OF THIS WAS ITSELF WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE FOR THE MECHANISM**: probing with `"$B" $a` under the harness shell produced exit 1 for four of the cases, because zsh does not word-split an unquoted parameter expansion, so `--version --zzz` arrived as ONE argument and clap rejected the whole token. Six rows of a table that measured nothing, and the giveaway was the error text quoting both words inside one pair of quotes. Re-run from a bash file with real argument vectors.
known_exposures.resolution: OPEN, and deliberately not resolved by the node that found it. Three things are entangled and only the first is mechanical. **(1)** The root intrinsics want a home in this table so that something can say what they do; there is no `root` entry today and adding one is a schema question. **(2)** `nothing_reaches_the_surface_that_is_not_in_the_table` passes right now with `-V` on the surface and undeclared, so **that guard's population excludes root flags** -- a hole in the instrument, found by a question about a feature rather than by the instrument. **(3)** Whether the swallow is a DEFECT or an INTRINSIC we accept is a ruling: clap's short-circuit is upstream behaviour and refusing it means intercepting before clap, which buys INV-02 conformance at the cost of reimplementing an intrinsic. **Third instance of the same class** -- `info`'s catch-all `args` slot and `st show`'s discarded `file` positional (AC-05.7) are the other two, and this one is on the command every user types first.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: None today: the generator renders the entries it is given and the root intrinsics are not entries. It gains one the moment (1) is answered -- a root row or an `intrinsics` block would need rendering, and until then **the rendered view is silently complete about a surface it does not cover.**
known_exposures.consequence_for_cc: **Do not build verbose build-metadata output onto `intent --version` without settling (3) first.** The flag would be parsed by a code path that clap exits before reaching, so the natural implementation is either unreachable or requires intercepting the intrinsic. Raised by cc, answered here: it is not an extension of an existing declared surface, because no row declares that surface -- so the choice is a flag declaration on a row that has to exist first, versus a new row, and the cheaper true statement is the former.

known_exposures.title: The register has no row for id normalisation because the question was never asked
known_exposures.detail: **A BEHAVIOUR SPANNING 21 VERBS ACROSS FIVE FAMILIES AND TWO DOORS WAS NEVER ASKED ABOUT IN THIS ARTEFACT.** vc's sweep: seven `normalis` hits in the rendered register, every one about STATUS normalisation or `organise`->`organize`. Id normalisation appears nowhere. It was not recorded-and-deferred, which a reader could act on -- it was unrecorded, and **the register's whole claim is that a row's existence means the question was asked.** The gap was found by an operator typing `intent st edit 59`, not by the artefact. **SO THE FINDING IS ABOUT THE POPULATION AND NOT THIS ROW**: nothing here establishes that id normalisation is the only such question, and the method that missed it was not id-specific.
known_exposures.resolution: AC-06.12 (2026-08-25) states the property and AT-06.12 covers it; landed at `58979836`. **The population question is SEPARATE and open, carried to hv by vc rather than closed here** -- a row added after the fact does not tell you what else was never asked.
known_exposures.it_happened: **YES, AND BY THE ONLY ROUTE THAT COULD HAVE FOUND IT.** hv typed `intent st new --start` and then `intent st edit 59` on 2026-08-25 and both refused -- the first on binary selection, the second on this. The register did not surface it in eleven days of parity work; **an operator typing an id the way operators type ids surfaced it in one command.** Recorded because the discovery ROUTE is the finding: this artefact enumerates what v2's surface DECLARES, and an accepted input spelling is not declared anywhere -- it is a property of how a command reads its argument, which no per-command scan of flags and arity can reach.
known_exposures.consequence_for_this_generator: **NOTHING IN THIS GENERATOR WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT AND NOTHING HERE NOW DOES.** The table's unit is the command and its declared flags; id normalisation is a property of ARGUMENT INTERPRETATION shared across 21 verbs and owned by none of them. A row per command cannot hold a fact that lives between commands. **So EXP-10 is closed for the instance and open for the class**, and adding a twelfth criterion did not narrow the population of questions never asked.

legal_pairs.gloss: The v2 command survives and v3 reproduces what v2 did. The default, and the largest class by a wide margin.
There is no v2 command. Both fields say so because the question `what becomes of it` does not apply to either axis -- this is one of the two pairs where the fields MUST agree.
The command survives with a defect fixed. `keep` is right precisely because a corrected command still SURVIVES; the correction is what `target.state` records.
The command survives; what v3 does with it is waiting on hv. The survival question is answered and the behaviour question is not, which is why two fields are better than one here.

The command does not ship. The second pair where the fields MUST agree, and the one with teeth: `Entry::is_shipped()` reads both and fails OPEN, so a single hand-edit to either field alone would ship a retired command.

The command survives with a deliberate behaviour change. `upgrade` is the only member (vc, 2026-08-16, citing D09) and it is the row that proves the two fields answer different questions -- it survives AND it behaves differently, and no single field can say both.
Neither question has been decided. `config` is the only member. The honest blank on both axes, which is the only pairing of `pending` that is coherent.

legal_pairs_note: THE PAIR IS THE DECLARED UNIT, AND A PAIR NOT LISTED ABOVE IS REFUSED. Ruled by vc 2026-08-16 in answer to the derivation question ic raised, and the answer is NO -- neither field is derived from the other. The contingency table makes derivation look obviously right: `target.state -> disposition` is a total function on the corpus, every one of the seven target states maps to exactly one disposition, so `disposition` carries strictly less information and is today a projection. Derive it anyway and three things break. (1) THE DRIFT REFUSAL GOES VACUOUS WHILE STILL READING AS A CHECK -- it would compare a computed value against the thing it was computed from, could never fire, and would sit in the file looking exactly as load-bearing as it does now. (2) IT DELETES THE ONLY REDUNDANCY `is_shipped()` HAS, and that function fails OPEN: two independently authored fields mean a single bad hand-edit is caught by comparing them, whereas one derived field makes the `&&` one test written twice. (3) THE FUNCTION IS A FACT ABOUT THE CURRENT CORPUS, NOT A LAW -- nothing forbids a `pending` disposition against a `corrected` target, and deriving would promote a coincidence to a rule without anyone deciding it should be one. The matrix is the alternative that keeps both fields authored while making a NEW combination an explicit decision rather than a silent widening: the previous refusal constrained only the two shared values, which admitted 17 of the 35 possible pairs while the corpus used 7. The concrete hole it closes is vc's: `disposition: pending` with `target.state: as-observed` passed every check that existed -- an honest blank against a confident claim that v3 reproduces v2 -- and those two cannot both be true of one row. POPULATION NOTE: the ruling was measured over 104 rows, which is `.families[].entries[]` alone and misses the 8-row top-level `new_surface[]` array. The full population is 112. The SET of pairs is identical either way and only the `new-surface` count moves, 11 to 19, so the ruling is untouched -- recorded because an incomplete basis that does not change the answer is the kind nobody catches.

key_classes.why: dc measured the declared-but-not-deserialized class to five instances and found no MECHANICAL discriminator between a key that must drive behaviour and a key that is prose -- not count (`read_or_mutate` is 112 rows and decides agent safety; `observed` is 93 rows and is a measurement block), not value type (`read_or_mutate` and `disposition_basis` are both strings). They are right that there is none, and right that the split is therefore AUTHORED. This is the authored answer, and it is scoped to the three leaf types on purpose.
key_classes.scope: `Entry`, `Flag` and `Arg` for the TOTALITY arm; `Target` is exempt from that one arm ONLY and is in scope for the declaration arms; `Table` is exempt from all of them. The original reasoning -- a register must accept prose nobody has typed yet -- is correct AT THE TOP LEVEL and was silently inherited by the leaves, which is where the bug was. **`Target` was then given a blanket exemption on a reason that argues for exactly one of the three arms.** Measured 2026-08-17: 42 distinct keys appear on `.target` across the corpus, 40 of them prose and 28 of THOSE on a single row, against 2 that code reads (`state` on 112 rows, `spelling` on 3). So the stated cost is real and it is a cost of TOTALITY -- enumerating 40 prose keys that grow every time someone records a reason is the over-refusing direction, the one that gets a guard bypassed rather than fixed. It says nothing about the two arms that bind the DECLARATION to the code, and those cost two list entries here. `Target.spelling` sat as a read key in no list at all, which is precisely the state the five lost fields were in, inside the one type the checks did not look at. **A consequence rather than a preference: because a totality-exempt type does not enumerate its notes, its declaration list is the WHOLE of its known set, so `nothing_is_read_that_the_canon_has_not_classified` is STRICTER on `Target` than on the three leaves.** On `Entry` a key may be read while classified a note (`Entry.v2`, and that costs nothing); on `Target` it must be refused, because with no note list there is no way to tell a note key from an unclassified one. Exempting a type from totality TIGHTENS what it may read.
key_classes.declaration: Code must read this key. If no type deserializes it, the behaviour it describes is either absent or hand-written to match by coincidence -- and the coincidence never surfaces, because agreement looks exactly like correctness.
key_classes.note: Prose, provenance or a measurement. No code reads it and none should. Adding one must stay free, or the register stops recording why things are the way they are.
key_classes.totality: Every key appearing on any `Entry`, `Flag` or `Arg` must be in exactly one list. `gen_dispatch_table.sh` refuses on an unclassified key, on a key in both, and on a classified key no row carries -- the third arm because a list that outlives its keys rots into a description of a file that no longer exists.

findings.ruling: NOTE, and this is a correction to the class rather than a member of it.
findings.why: It was grouped with `Flag.required` / `default` / `value` as one class. Those three each had ONE type and one meaning, and cc has since built all three. `accepts` has FOUR rows and FOUR grammars: `st list --status` is a synonym table with normalisation rules (`wip|in progress -> WIP; ...`), `critic --severity-min` is a clean pipe-separated enum, `learn --category` is a comma list with the default marked inline (`footgun (default), worked, failed`), and `init --lang` is a sentence with an example. **Nothing could parse this, so it cannot be a declaration** -- a declaration with four grammars is prose that happens to be regular sometimes.
findings.residue: The real gap it points at: `Arg` has `values` (structured, 11 rows, read), and `Flag` has NO equivalent. Three of these four flags have genuinely enumerable value sets clap could validate. Promoting them means adding a structured `values` to `Flag` and rewriting the four, not deserializing this key. Not done here -- it is new surface, and this block's job was to classify what exists.

findings.ruling: DECLARATION -- dc's fifth instance, confirmed. `pub struct Arg` has no `default` and the canon declares one on 8 rows.
findings.why: It decides behaviour: `intent todo` bare runs `list`, correctly, from hand-written code with no mechanical link to the declaration it happens to match. Seven of the eight sit on families that answer `not implemented yet` today, so seven get hand-implemented from a declaration nothing reads.
findings.trap: **The 8 rows are 7 literals and 1 sentence, and a naive `default: Option<String>` would ship the sentence as a value.** Five are subcommand defaults (`list`), two are enum defaults (`info`), and `init`'s reads `the current directory name` -- a DESCRIPTION OF A COMPUTATION, not a literal. Deserialize this key as written and `intent init` names the project `the current directory name`. Either that row gets a computed-default spelling distinct from a literal one, or it is excluded by name and says why.

findings.ruling: NOTE by classification, VESTIGIAL by inspection -- the honest answer is that it should be deleted.
findings.why: One row carries it: `st`, `kind: family`. Family-ness is derivable from the path set -- a path is a family root when another declared path is it plus a space -- and that derivation was run against this table on 2026-08-16 to split the withheld-from-MCP rows, giving 13 roots without consulting this key once. A structural claim that one row states and a hundred and eleven leave to inference is not carrying anything. Classified `note` so the totality check passes today; flagged here so the classification is not mistaken for an endorsement.

key_classes.closes_one_half_only: **This split does NOT close the declared-but-not-deserialized class, and saying so here rather than letting the next instance discover it.** (vc, from issue 0040.) There are two mechanisms and classification plus a serde check sees only the first. **(a) Declared in JSON, no Rust field** -- serde drops it in silence; a flatten or key-set check catches this, and it is what `aliases` and `Arg.default` were. **(b) Declared in JSON, the Rust field EXISTS and deserializes correctly, and no code CONSUMES the value.** `Config.st_prefix` is the measured instance: declared with a serde default of `ST`, three occurrences in the workspace and all three its own declaration, while `facade.rs` allocates ids with a hardcoded `ST{:04}` and `legacy.rs` recognises threads with a hardcoded `starts_with(ST)` -- and v2 honours the field in six places. **Nothing catches (b): the key never lands in a `rest` map, so a flatten check reports agreement, and `dead_code` does not fire because a `pub` field on a `pub` struct in a lib crate is reachable by definition.** Recorded here because a check's error message is where its readers learn what it does, and nothing verifies that message against its behaviour -- a lesson this register earned the hard way and would otherwise have re-learned. **vc's sharper discriminator, worth adopting if this list is ever reorganised: the question is not `is this key read` but `does a consumer exist and encode the value another way`.** It separates all three of `Config`'s unread fields where count and type separate none -- `st_prefix` is a defect (consumers exist and hardcode), `author` is correct (D02 removed the verblock, the consumer is gone by ruling), `languages` is pending (its consumers are unwired).

target.why: No `note` list, deliberately, and its absence is load-bearing rather than an omission -- see `scope`. `Target` is exempt from the totality arm, so its 40 prose keys are not enumerated; that makes `declaration` the entire known set for this type and the read-side arm correspondingly strict. A key this type deserializes that is not listed here is refused, whether it is prose or a contract, because nothing here can tell them apart.

populations.why: THE FOUR POPULATIONS, ENUMERATED, so no consumer has to re-derive one. `.families[].entries[]` reads like the command surface and is not it, in BOTH directions at once: too narrow, because it omits the 8 top-level `new_surface[]` rows and all 8 ship; too wide, because it includes the 5 rows dispositioned `retire`, which the binary does not contain. 104 against 112 against 107, three apart with opposite signs, so no count-based sanity check flinches -- which is how the same wrong population was hand-written five times in one week. **The fix is not vigilance and it is not a shared library either: a sourced library closes the class only for callers that source it, and nothing makes them.** `lib_surface.sh` was built as the one home and then sat beside `implemented_check.sh`'s own list and four inline walks in `surface_check.sh`, none of which sourced it, so it added a home rather than removing three. This block is the one home; the library reads it, and `gen_dispatch_table.sh` refuses when it disagrees with the corpus. The redundancy is deliberate -- `retired` is `declared` minus `shipped` and `probeable` is `shipped` minus `not_probed` -- because a consumer that has to subtract is a consumer that is computing. `Entry::is_shipped()` in the binary is NOT replaced by a lookup: it fails OPEN across two fields and is the only thing stopping a single hand-edit from shipping a retired command, and a list is edited by people who believe they are editing data. It stays a predicate and a Rust test binds it to `shipped`. Order is table order. **`not_probed` CARRIES ITS OWN REASONS BECAUSE ITS PREDECESSOR LOST A MEMBER TO ITS NAME** (vc, 2026-08-17, on their own `SURFACE_NONRETURNING`): the four are excluded for TWO different reasons -- two never return, two write outside the sandbox -- and `claude upgrade`, which returns perfectly well and installs into the operator's real `~/.claude`, fell out of a list whose name was only ever entitled to define one of the two. `claude start` survived only because it satisfies both readings, so the surviving two-word row made the list look complete. A key named for one reason cannot hold members admitted for another, and the correction is not a better name but a member that states its own grounds. **AND THE CRITERION IS NARROWER THAN `writes outside the sandbox`, WHICH IS THE GUARD AGAINST THIS LIST GOING SHORT A SECOND TIME** (vc, 2026-08-17, who checked their own fix by CORRESPONDENCE rather than reading it -- all four populations diffed member-by-member, not by count, because counts pass on a block with the right arithmetic and the wrong rows). Two SIBLINGS write destructively to the operator's real home -- `plugin_remove_target` is `rm -rf "$HOME/.claude/skills/$1"` at `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_skills:73` and `rm -f "$HOME/.claude/agents/$1.md"` at `intent_claude_subagents:79` -- and BOTH are correctly probeable, because bare `claude skills` and bare `claude subagents` dispatch to help (`""|help|-h|--help)` at :406 and :733 respectively) so the probe never reaches the destructive verb. `intent_claude_upgrade` has no such arm: it is a LEAF, and bare RUNS it. **So the criterion is `writes outside the sandbox WHEN INVOKED BARE, because bare is how the probe invokes`** -- and a criterion stated more broadly than the one actually applied is precisely what let a member fall out of this list last time. If a row ever gains a bare side effect, or a leaf is added under a name that reads like a family, the list goes short again in silence. Verified at HEAD by ic before recording. **THIRD ARRAY, AND IT IS EMPTY TODAY (ic, 2026-08-22): `families_outstanding` is a top-level array alongside `families` and `new_surface`.** A union of the other two is correct ONLY while this one has zero members, and nothing announces the day it does not -- a walk that is right by accident reads exactly like a walk that is right by construction. **Consult this block; do not union the arrays you happen to know about.**

no_op_note: **`no_op` STATES WHAT A VERB PRINTS WHEN IT IS ASKED FOR THE STATE THE ENTITY IS ALREADY IN**, and it exists because nothing else in this register could say it. Issue 0050: hv's self-loop ruling gave the facade `Outcome::AlreadyThere`, nineteen `render.rs` arms discard it and print the movement message anyway, and two read it -- so `intent todo done ST0001` answers `was already done` while `intent st done ST0001`, the call it DELEGATES to, answers `done`. The table declared help, flags and exit codes and had no notation for that difference, so no parity tool could hold the renderer to anything. **TWO FIELDS, NOT ONE, BECAUSE THE TABLE ALREADY SPLITS THAT WAY.** `observed.no_op` is v2's behaviour and `target.no_op` is v3's. A single field would record the answer and lose the question, which is the one thing a parity register must not do -- and `observed` is NOT empty here: v2 has two no-op arms, `ok: issue <ID> already CLOSED` (bin/intent_issues:282) and `skipped: <ID> already in progress` (bin/intent_st:635), in DIFFERENT prefixes. **Everything else v2 does on a no-op is a repeated write that happens to land on the same value**, which is a materially different thing from a no-op and is why each such row says so rather than saying `ok`. **WHERE THE v2 HALF IS ABSENT, IT IS ABSENT UNAMBIGUOUSLY.** `observed` exists on a row exactly when `target.state` is not `new-surface` -- true across all 26 rows of the population and mechanical, not a convention -- so a missing `observed.no_op` already means `v2 had no such command` and needs no sentinel of its own. The requirement is therefore: `target.no_op` on every row of the population, `observed.no_op` on every row of it that has an `observed` block. **THREE SHAPES, AND THE THIRD IS THE POINT** (cc's argument, adopted): absent must never mean both `no self-loop is possible here` and `nobody has looked`. So a row in `populations.self_loop` always carries the key, and a value beginning `unexamined` is a declaration of ignorance rather than the silence that reads like coverage. `new-surface` says v2 had no antecedent, so there is nothing to be faithful to. **EVERY `target` VALUE DESCRIBES HEAD, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN READ.** The ruled voice is `ok: <subject> already <state>` (vc, 2026-08-17, over the participle `was already <verb>`, on the grounds that a no-op reports a PRESENT condition and that the participle only coincides with the state when verb and state share a word -- `st hold` breaks it immediately). **It SHIPPED at `d0f345b5`**, so the rows cite that commit instead of the ruling. **Both halves of every row were obtained by driving the verb TWICE through a real binary** -- v3 from a release build of a `git archive` EXTRACT, v2.19.0 through the `intent` on PATH -- because the day's repeated lesson is that reading a source file answers a question adjacent to the one being asked. That method is not decoration: it is the only reason three of these rows are right. **`ac rescope` and `ac reinstate` were handed over as `ok: <AC> already unsatisfied | already computed` and in fact REFUSE at exit 1** (issue 0053) -- the announced value was reasoned correctly from `AcState::entry(kind)`, which is what the success arm passes the setter, and the self-loop never reaches that arm. **`todo notdone` and `todo toggle` have no reachable self-loop at all**, refusing unconditionally before any state is read, which is a third shape the `unexamined` sentinel could not have expressed. **And `at na` prints a state token, `n-a`, that appears in no canon file** -- v2 writes `n/a` in the row grammar and prints it back. None of the three is visible from the source of the verb alone, and all three would have entered the register as clean `ok:` lines had the values been transcribed. **The extract is not ceremony and the first attempt at this needed it.** The initial build was taken from a working tree that `git status` reported clean, and it was; a peer then began editing `render.rs` in the same shared checkout and something rebuilt the binary at a path this measurement was still reading. **Both binaries carry the same name, the same size to the eye, and no record of which tree they came from** -- the only thing that separated them was an mtime 31 seconds apart, which proves order and not content. Every value here was therefore re-driven against a binary built from `git archive HEAD`, whose `native/` is bit-identical to `b7e60fc5` (`git diff --stat b7e60fc5..HEAD -- native/ surface/` is empty), and all 27 reproduced unchanged. **The rule this leaves: in a shared checkout a clean `git status` licenses a build, not a measurement taken later against its output.**
arg_values_note: **`values` ON A NON-SUBCOMMAND SLOT IS A DECLARATION, NOT A CONSTRAINT. NOTHING IN THE PARSER READS IT, AND ITS ENFORCEMENT IS THE FACADE'S.** `spine.rs` reads `values` in exactly two places: to expand a `kind: subcommand` slot into real subcommands (`:349-351`), and to resolve a slot's default (`:764`). **There is no `value_parser` built from a positional's `values`**, so `critic`'s `lang`, `st show`'s `file` and `wp rescope`'s `size` all declare their permitted values here and are all validated one layer down. That is a fine arrangement -- a register may declare more than clap enforces when something below enforces it -- and it is only fine while something does. **IT IS WRITTEN HERE, IN THE TABLE, BECAUSE THE TABLE IS WHAT AN IMPLEMENTER READS** (cc's point, and they are right that the spine is the wrong home for it). The way this becomes a real defect is not a decision anyone takes: it is a `values` array written on a row by an author who assumes clap has it, read by an implementer who assumes the same, and enforced by nobody. **That is precisely what nearly happened with `wp rescope` on 2026-08-17** -- ic wrote the array, told cc it built the enum, and the correction arrived before the render arm did. Nothing about the table caught it and nothing about the table would have; what caught it was the timing. So the note exists to make the next author's assumption wrong on the page rather than in the binary. **A row declaring `values` therefore owes an exit-1 arm for an unreadable value**, and the refusal should name the permitted set rather than only rejecting the input -- a bare parse error blames the spelling without saying what the spellings are. **CORRECTED 2026-08-17: THIS NOTE SAID THREE SLOTS AND THERE ARE FIVE.** The non-subcommand slots carrying `values` are `critic`'s `lang`, **`st show`'s `file`**, **`st edit`'s `file`**, `wp rescope`'s `size`, and **`config`'s `backup.schedule`** (`hourly`/`daily`/`weekly`). The note named three: it missed the SECOND `file` -- two rows declare the same slot name with different value sets, and enumerating by name collapses them to one -- and it missed `backup.schedule` entirely, which no Rust source in the workspace mentions by key or by value. **THREE COUNTS, THREE ENUMERATORS, EACH SHORT OF THE NEXT, and none of the three was careless** (cc, 2026-08-17). This note said 3 by naming slots in prose. cc's probe said 4 by walking `entry.args` and `entry.flags` -- two container keys named by hand, and the fifth lives in a third. The true 5 comes from recursively walking the raw table TEXT for any object carrying a `values` array. **And the typed model cannot see it at all: `dispatch::Flag` has no `values` field, so a `values` array on a flag row deserialises into nothing** -- an enumerator built on the struct is structurally unable to report a slot the struct drops. That is why `declared_values_are_enforced.rs` reads the raw text rather than `dispatch::table()`, and why every slot must now carry a driven disposition -- Enforced, Unwired, Unenforced(issue), Planned(surface) -- with a new undeclared one FAILING. **The lesson is not that the count was wrong; it is that a population reported by an enumerator is the enumerator's subject, not the population**, and three independent ones went short in three different ways on a set of five.
